routes.label: Divide the distance in a ratio

question: Cities \(A\) and \(B\) are \(45\) miles apart. Alicia lives in \(A\) and Beth lives in \(B.\) Alicia bikes towards \(B\) at \(18\) miles per hour. Leaving at the same time, Beth bikes toward \(A\) at \(12\) miles per hour. How many miles from City \(A\) will they be when they meet?
solution:
Both riders reduce the gap between them, so together they close it at
\[
18+12=30\text{ miles per hour}.
\]
Closing the \(45\)-mile gap takes
\[
\frac{45}{30}=\frac32\text{ hours}.
\]
Alicia starts at City \(A\), so the meeting point is the distance she rides from \(A\):
\[
18\cdot\frac32=\boxed{27}\text{ miles},
\]
choice E.

solutionMethods.explanation:
The riders travel for the same amount of time, so their distances are in the same ratio as their speeds:
\[
18:12=3:2.
\]
Their distances together make up the \(45\) miles between the cities. Divide \(45\) into \(3+2=5\) equal parts, each measuring \(45\div5=9\) miles. Alicia travels three of these parts, so they meet
\[
3\cdot9=\boxed{27}\text{ miles from City }A,
\]
choice E.
